p01.why: A pointer to member is not a valid shift operand.

p02.why: The type of nullptr is not a valid shift operand.

p03.why: Unsigned left shifts keep the low 32 bits, so every assertion holds.

p04.why: a << 1 is a prvalue, so & cannot take its address.

p05.why: The count is -1 at run time, which is undefined, and the undefined sanitizer stops the program.

p06.why: The char operand promotes to int before the shift, so a count of 20 is in range.

p07.why: A pointer is not a valid shift operand.

p08.why: S has no conversion and no operator<<, so the class operand is not valid.

p09.why: A floating-point left operand is not valid.

p10.why: A constant count of 33 is past the width of int; Clang and GCC warn by default and -Werror makes that an error.

p11.why: A left shift keeps the low 32 bits even when the sign changes, so 1 << 31 is INT_MIN and 3 << 30 is -(1 << 30).

p12.why: The result type is the promoted left operand alone: int, int, unsigned, long, int.

p13.why: A floating-point right operand is not valid.

p14.why: A constant negative count draws a default warning, and -Werror makes it an error.

p15.why: A scoped enumeration is not a valid shift operand.

p16.why: A count of 32 equals the width of int, which is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p17.why: Right shift rounds toward negative infinity, so -7 >> 1 is -4 and -1 stays -1.

p18.why: A negative count is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p19.why: 13 / 4 rounds down to 3, and the top bit of the unsigned value shifts down to 1.

p20.why: Unscoped enumerations, bool, and char are valid operands, and long long has room for a shift of 40.

p21.why: A count of 32 equals the width of unsigned, which is undefined even for a right shift, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p22.why: The left operand is evaluated first, so the order is 1 then 2, and 1 << 3 is 8.

p23.why: Left shifts of negative values are defined and multiply by a power of two.

p24.why: The count is 32, the width of int, which is undefined, and the undefined sanitizer stops the program.

p25.why: Shifts group left to right, bind looser than + and tighter than <, so each assertion holds.
